papers.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.
papers.title_ja: 言語モデルが言語モデルの改善を学習する
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、LLMを用いたAI研究の自動化、特に言語モデル開発における再帰的自己改善を目的とするLM2LMフレームワークを提案する。高コストな実実験フィードバックの代わりに、実験記録から提案の効果を予測する「研究ワールドモデル（RWM）」を報酬モデルとして用いることで、強化学習（RL）の計算コストを大幅に削減する。さらに、RWMの予測が偏る問題を解決するため、高評価提案を実際に実行し、その結果をコンテキストに追加する動的更新機構を導入した。8つのLM開発環境での評価により、LM2LMはGPT-6-solを上回る性能を示し、データ生成コストを33%削減しつつ、未知のモデルファミリーへも汎化できることを実証した。

papers.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling
papers.summary: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.

papers.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
papers.summary: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. Across six three-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU. It also supports zero-shot super-resolution and efficient closed-form spatial derivatives. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29.2-million-node MAST-U tokamak model.

papers.title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
papers.summary: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Mat\'ern-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.
papers.title_ja: 逆問題への応用を伴う多層ガウス過程

papers.title: Regime-Aware Coupled Orchestration of Neural Operator Specialists for Multiphysics Dynamics
papers.summary: Real-world physics often unfolds over a variety of characteristic lengths and time scales. These non-uniformities are among the main reasons numerical simulations remain expensive when used predictively on practical systems: the same computational domain can contain smooth transport, vortical structures, thin interfaces, reaction fronts, and rapidly relaxing regions. Neural operators are attractive surrogates for such problems. However, a single architecture is still expected to represent all these local behaviours with a single set of weights and a single inductive bias. In this work, we introduce the regime-aware coupled neural orchestrator (RCNO), a framework that learns to distribute and connect a library of local operator specialists in space and time. For every patch, an orchestrator builds a causal query from the current fields, neighbouring halo values, local regime features, patch identity, activity level, and case parameters. The nine expert embeddings exchange two rounds of query-conditioned message passing before an edge-biased cross-attention stage produces a dispatch distribution that can be evaluated sparsely. Local predictions are assembled into a global field and projected onto system-specific physical constraints. A seam-aware extension additionally learns residual corrections across internal patch interfaces. We apply the same orchestration architecture to two qualitatively different systems: reacting flow and Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes (CHNS) dynamics. The results show that useful operator specialisation exists across local regimes, that the advantage of conditional composition increases as the spatial decomposition becomes finer, and, on reacting flow, that explicitly treating patch interfaces improves continuity, PDE consistency, and rollout accuracy.

papers.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
papers.summary: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. In Qwen3-30B-A3B this loss is made at the two chat-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek-V2-Lite at the first 8-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage. Reduction changes the first token's attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full. On real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts, placing them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while placing them at random in the documents is about 3 points worse (two of five prespecified primary comparisons; the others were undecided or not run). Because the answer boundary always ends a single-turn prompt, and DeepSeek's loss was no longer detectable once its instruction moved away from the start, the sensitive tokens lay at the prompt ends in every sensitive layout we found, so rules that keep the ends are not distinguished from rules that read application marks. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts and not at 2K tokens.

papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) モデルの推論コスト削減策である「プリフィル時のルーティングエキスパート削減」が、特に短い回答タスクにおいてどのような性能劣化を引き起こすかを分析する。4つのMoEモデルファミリーを対象に、トークン・レイヤー・アテンションパスの介入実験を行い、損失の多くが「回答形式の崩壊（簡潔な回答を止めること）」であること、そしてその原因がプロンプトの先頭やチャットテンプレート直前などの特定位置のトークンにあることを特定した。これらの敏感な位置のみフルエキスパートを維持する戦略により、F1スコアをほぼ維持しつつ、11KトークンプロンプトにおいてTime to First Token (TTFT) を約14%短縮できることを示した。

papers.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
papers.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: https://eliezer318.github.io/SPOT-dLLM/
papers.title_ja: SPOT: 順序予測による拡散言語モデルの投機的デコーディング強化
papers.summary_ja: 拡散言語モデル（DLM）における速度と品質のトレードオフを解決するため、トークン生成の順序を予測する手法SPOTを提案する。既存の自己回帰モデル向け投機的デコーディングをDLMに適用する際、生成位置の決定が課題であったが、本手法は小型モデルで候補ツリーを生成し、ターゲットモデルが一度のパスで検証する。これにより、ターゲットモデルの計算パスを最大6.8倍削減し、標準デコーディング比で最大3.2倍のスループット向上を実現した。さらに、学習済みドラフターが異なるDLM間でも転移可能であることを示した。

papers.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: A gradient-based solver that enforces a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification uses a smooth approximation of its quantitative semantics, the robustness. In safety-critical trajectory optimization, this approximation must have two properties. First, it must be sound, that is, nonnegative only on trajectories that satisfy the specification. Second, at each temporal operator, the weight of its gradient on the violating samples must stay bounded away from zero, however long the horizon. The approximations in use, including the log-sum-exp, its sound variant, and the generalized-mean robustness, do not have both. We introduce lower approximations of the minimum and the maximum whose gradients are sparsemax projections, and we prove that the robustness built from them has both. It lies below the exact robustness and is therefore sound, and its error has a bound that is independent of the number of samples and known before optimization. The gradient of each approximation is exactly zero on every sample beyond a data-dependent threshold, so the weight on violating samples a gap beyond the others has a positive lower bound at every horizon. On a planar unicycle and on a seven-joint manipulator beside a person in simulation, the log-sum-exp approximation is positive on a violating trajectory. As the horizon of the manipulator's task grows from 10 to 80 s, the gradient weight of the sound variant on the violating samples falls from 0.22 to 0.04, while that of sparsemax stays at 1. In a constrained trajectory optimization of the unicycle, the constraint on the log-sum-exp robustness returns a violating trajectory, whereas the constraint on the sparsemax robustness returns a trajectory that satisfies the specification with the required margin.

papers.title: When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration
papers.summary: Calibrating expensive engineering simulators requires tuning model parameters to match reference data, a process heavily constrained by computational costs. This study investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs), conditioned on physical diagnostic descriptions of simulation errors, can propose informative parameter updates more efficiently than conventional derivative-free optimizers. We test this on a cylinder-wake Large-Eddy Simulation and a damped-oscillator inverse problem. Physics-labeled prompts are evaluated against four text ablations (removed, anonymized, padded, misdirected) and standard optimizers (Nelder-Mead, Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and random search). Results demonstrate a strong early semantic advantage: the first physics-informed LLM proposal improves the initial design in 23 of 25 trials. After five evaluations, the median calibration error is 21.9 times lower than physics-free controls. However, this advantage is transient - disappearing by fifteen evaluations - and inherent LLM decoder variability yields a 9.8-fold performance spread. To address this, we introduce a hybrid workflow that uses the LLM as a warm-start, passing accumulated evaluations to a conventional optimizer. This two-stage numerical continuation policy reaches target accuracy in just 9 simulator runs, outperforming the LLM alone (12 runs), Nelder-Mead (17 runs), and Bayesian optimization (>60 runs). Supported by sensitivity analysis validating the test cases, this hybrid physics-labeled LLM scheme proves highly effective as a calibration agent under strict evaluation budgets.

papers.title: Physics-informed Neural Networks Based on the Fokker-Planck Model for Rarefied Gas Flows
papers.summary: Rarefied nonequilibrium flows are described by the Boltzmann equation, which can be solved using stochastic particle or deterministic methods. With advances in computing, data-assisted physics-informed neural networks have been widely used for flow prediction by combining governing equations with measured or computed data. Data-free PINNs do not require such training data and have been widely studied for continuum flows, but their application to rarefied flows remains limited. This study develops a data-free Fokker-Planck physics-informed neural network (FP-PINN) to describe rarefied nonequilibrium flows. The physics loss is constructed from the ellipsoidal statistical Fokker-Planck (ES-FP) equation using a velocity distribution function (VDF) closure and moment projection. The FP-PINN is evaluated for a steady one-dimensional Mach 10 normal shock. The FP-PINN results agree with the numerical ES-FP results, with errors below $1\%$. Compared with the particle ES-FP results, the FP-PINN predicts a sharper shock structure with errors up to $17\%$. This difference is attributed to the VDF closure and moment projection.
papers.title_ja: 希薄気体流のためのフォッカー・プランクモデルに基づく物理情報ニューラルネットワーク

papers.title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
papers.summary: Reconstructing flow fields from sparse and noisy measurements becomes particularly challenging when data are completely absent from dynamically critical regions, such as the vortex-formation region of a wake. Conventional interpolation and numerical reconstruction methods generally require sufficient spatial or boundary information, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can also face difficulties when sparse and noisy observations provide little or no supervision in the region of interest. To address this gap, we propose a Fourier-feature-embedded complex-valued physics-informed convolutional residual network (FCV-PICRN) for sparse, gappy, and noisy flow-field reconstruction. The framework integrates Fourier features for oscillatory and multiscale structures, complex-valued representations for coupled amplitude--phase learning, and convolutional residual blocks constrained by the Navier--Stokes equations. The method is first verified using the Taylor--Green vortex at $Re=100$ and then evaluated for the cylinder wake at $Re=100$. Three severe missing-data configurations are imposed in the dynamically sensitive wake: a large hole, a large truncation, and a plus-shaped gap extending in both streamwise and transverse directions. These gaps are further combined with additive Gaussian and multiplicative speckle noise. Despite having no supervised velocity data inside the excluded regions, FCV-PICRN reconstructs velocity, pressure, and vorticity with high structural similarity index (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and remains robust under Gaussian noise up to $20\%$. Finally, for forced two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence with $5\%$ Gaussian noise, FCV-PICRN yields lower reconstruction errors than a conventional PINN. These results demonstrate robust physics-informed reconstruction of severely incomplete and noisy flows across laminar and turbulent regimes.
papers.title_ja: スパースかつ欠損・ノイズを含む流れ場再構成のための、Fourier特徴量埋め込み型複素数値物理情報畳み込み残差ネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、観測データが欠損しノイズを含む流れ場の再構成問題を解決するため、Fourier特徴量と複素数値表現を組み合わせた物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の一種であるFCV-PICRNを提案する。Navier-Stokes方程式による制約と畳み込み残差ブロックを用いることで、渦生成領域などの動的に重要な部分のデータが完全に欠落しても、速度・圧力・渦度を高精度に再構成できることを示した。Taylor-Green渦や円柱尾流、乱流のシミュレーションにおいて、従来のPINNや補間法よりも高い構造類似度（SSIM）とピーク信号雑音比（PSNR）を達成し、20%のガウスノイズ下でも頑健性を示した。

papers.title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning
papers.summary: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. We evaluate the framework across 2D and 3D rigid- body planning tasks and non-prehensile manipulation through object pushing in diverse environments. Results show substantial improvements in planning success and inference efficiency over physics-informed neural planning baselines, while remaining competitive with classical sampling-based planners at significantly lower planning times. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of both the learned representation and the proposed planning strategy. Finally, closed-loop pushing experiments under execution deviations and external disturbances demonstrate that fast replanning enables reactive and adaptive task execution.
papers.title_ja: 剛体運動とマニピュレーション計画のための形状認識型ニューラルタイムフィールド
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、剛体の並進と回転の幾何学的制約を明示的に考慮した、物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）ベースの運動計画フレームワーク「Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields」を提案する。再利用可能な移動時間（コスト）表現を学習し、サンプリングベースのプランナーと組み合わせることで、複雑な環境下での計画精度と推論効率を向上させる。2D/3D剛体計画および物体プッシュによる非把持マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、既存のPINNベース手法より大幅に性能が向上し、古典的サンプリング手法と同等以上の成功率をより短い計画時間で達成したことを示す。さらに、実行誤差や外部擾乱下でのクローズドループ実験により、高速な再計画による適応的タスク実行能力を実証している。

papers.title: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces
papers.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) over discrete spaces is challenging due to missing gradients and the sparsity of valid solutions. Latent-space BO sidesteps both issues by fitting a surrogate in the latent space of a generative model, which however substantially complicates the direct incorporation of domain knowledge that is naturally expressed in the original discrete space. In this work, we instead combine a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space, where inductive biases such as domain-specific kernels can be readily incorporated. Rather than maximizing the acquisition function over the discrete design space, our method samples candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function. To recover useful gradients for sampling, we embed this tilted distribution into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior-averaged acquisition function. This leads to \emph{acquisition function guided generation} (AFGG), which we instantiate with a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow. Across a broad suite of molecular benchmarks, the diffusion model variant performs on par with leading BO methods, while the flow model variant outperforms state-of-the-art methods in most cases and remains highly competitive otherwise. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/afgg.
papers.title_ja: 離散空間におけるベイズ最適化のための取得関数ガイド生成
papers.summary_ja: 離散空間におけるベイズ最適化（BO）の課題である勾配の欠如と有効解の希少性を解決するため、事前学習済み生成モデルとデータ空間上のサロゲートモデルを組み合わせる手法を提案する。取得関数によって傾けられた分布から候補をサンプリングし、拡散ブリッジを用いて滑らかな後验平均取得関数を導出することで、効率的な探索を実現する。分子ベンチマークにおいて、拡散モデル版は既存の最先端手法と同等の性能を示し、正規化フロー版は多くのケースで既存手法を上回る結果を得た。

papers.title: Prune the Leaky Neurons: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in Fine-Tuned LLMs via Joint-Embedding-Guided Pruning
papers.summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on proprietary records enables domain adaptation but introduces two challenges: (i) privacy leakage of memorized private data, such as personally identifiable information (PII), and (ii) balancing private data removal with utility preservation. Existing defenses, including data sanitization and differential privacy, often degrade performance, while privacy-neuron editing lacks a PII-free reference to distinguish identity-specific neurons from those supporting useful text. We propose JEPA-Prune, a post-hoc neuron pruning framework guided by a model trained exclusively on PII-free views. Alongside the fine-tuned private model, JEPA-Prune, trains a public model on surrogate and masked views of the same records using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), capturing domain knowledge without identifiers. A cross-model representation probe quantifies deviations between private representations of leaked records and this PII-free reference. Integrated gradients and a scale-invariant specificity score then identify PII-responsive neurons, which are pruned without retraining. Experiments show that pruning just 1.6% of neurons reduces PII inference accuracy by up to 7.4x and PII extraction recall by up to 13.9x, while keeping unseen-text perplexity within 16% of that of the unpruned model for most LLMs. In contrast, privacy-neuron editing increases perplexity by at least 26x.
papers.title_ja: 漏洩ニューロンの剪定：共同埋め込み誘導型剪定によるファインチューニング済みLLMのプライベートデータ漏洩の軽減
papers.summary_ja: ファインチューニング済みLLMにおける個人識別情報（PII）の漏洩を、性能劣化を抑えつつ軽減する事後処理フレームワーク「JEPA-Prune」を提案する。PIIを含まないサロゲートデータで訓練したJEPAモデルを参照基準とし、統合勾配と尺度不変特異性スコアを用いてPIIに反応するニューロンを特定・剪定する。実験では、ニューロンのわずか1.6%を剪定するだけでPII推論精度を最大7.4倍、抽出リコールを最大13.9倍低減しつつ、既知テキストのパープレキシティは未剪定モデルの16%以内で維持できた。従来のプライバシーニューロン編集法がパープレキシティを26倍以上悪化させるのに対し、本手法はユーティリティとプライバシーのバランスを大幅に改善する。

papers.title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
papers.summary: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. Firstly, we design separate sub-networks for each medium with learnable parameters to automatically learn interface positions, so that the domain decomposition is physically consistent, and the contact discontinuity at the interface is naturally sharp. Secondly, the Euler equations with artificial viscosity are solved to enhance robustness when handling problems involving shock waves. Lastly, the scaling invariance of the Euler equations is exploited to facilitate the solution of high pressure ratio problems. Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems demonstrate the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in simulating multi-medium flows.
papers.title_ja: PINN-LPCDD: 圧縮性多相流のための学習可能かつ物理的に一貫した領域分割を用いた物理情報ニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 圧縮性多相流のシミュレーションにおいて、PINNが抱える界面位置の特定困難や不連続性の近似精度の低さ、高圧比問題への対応難を解決するフレームワークを提案する。各媒体ごとにサブネットワークを設計し、学習可能なパラメータを用いて界面位置を自動学習することで、物理的に一貫した領域分割を実現し、界面での接触不連続性を自然にシャープに表現する。さらに、人工粘性を用いたオイラー方程式の解法と、オイラー方程式のスケーリング不変性を活用することで、衝撃波を含む問題や高圧比問題におけるロバスト性を向上させる。空気-空気、空気-ヘリウム、空気-水、空気-R22などの数値実験により、本手法が多相流のシミュレーションにおいて許容できる精度を持つことを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNという関心領域の手法を、物理的に一貫した領域分割という新しいアプローチで拡張しており、高度な物理シミュレーションへの適用可能性が高い。

papers.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
papers.summary: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number. We map this boundary, and the family obtained by moving the elastic axis, with coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping coefficient trained by batch active learning, and split conformal prediction on independent random simulations, which turns the surrogate into stability calls with a distribution-free error rate. Three failure modes of time-domain damping labels that leave no trace in the residuals are documented, and the half-degree mean incidence left by the common one-degree start is shown to raise the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 64 of 65 independent runs correctly, and calibrated calls are wrong in at most 1.6% of cases. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs show that the fold exists only for elastic axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge; it closes between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed against the solver loads and the growth rate within a few per cent, explain the boundary. The lower branch is crossed through the reduced frequency at unchanged shock phase. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge, and moving the elastic axis aft brings the pivot of the flutter mode towards the section, so that the damping of the supersonic surface falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.
papers.title_ja: 弾性軸が音速域のフラッター境界を折り畳む仕組み：衝撃波エネルギー伝達と共形較正アクティブラーニング
papers.summary_ja: 音速域におけるフラッター境界の複雑な構造（折り畳み）を、非定常Euler方程式シミュレーションとガウス過程サロゲートモデルを用いて高精度にマッピングする。バッチアクティブラーニングで訓練されたサロゲートに共形予測を適用し、分布非依存のエラー率保証付き安定性判定を実現した。さらに、時間領域ダンピングラベルの失敗モードや初期条件の影響を定量化し、弾性軸位置と衝撃波エネルギー伝達による境界の閉鎖メカニズムを物理的に解明した。

papers.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) encode substantial factual knowledge. Yet, estimating confidence in factual claims reliably remains challenging. We study likelihood-based factual confidence from the complementary perspectives of discrimination and calibration across multilingual factual statements. Specifically, we instantiate contrastive generative likelihoods as Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE), which compares the likelihood of the same claim under competing factual and non-factual conditions, and derive its probabilistic counterpart, the Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP). We show analytically that CFP calibration depends on the differential error between the two surrogate conditionals, allowing errors shared across them to cancel and yield tighter calibration bounds. Empirically, CFP substantially improves calibration while maintaining factual discrimination comparable to its strongest competitor. Nonetheless, discrimination is uniformly weak across methods in lower-resource languages, which simultaneously undermines the utility of the measured calibration. To this end, we interpret a likelihood geometry, within which an evidence-bearing direction is induced, along with an orthogonal evidence-invariant direction. In our investigation, we selectively align target-language claims with stronger English evidence only along the factual-evidence direction, improving discrimination and open-ended factual generation without target-language labels.
papers.title_ja: 対比による真実：言語モデルの尤度に基づく較正された事実証拠
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の事実認識における信頼度推定を改善するため、対比生成尤度（CFE）と確率論的対応物である対比事実事後確率（CFP）を提案する。CFPは、事実と非事実の条件間の差分誤差を利用することで、共有誤差を打ち消し、較正の境界を厳密にする理論的根拠を持つ。実験では、CFPが事実識別性能を維持しつつ較正精度を大幅に向上させることを示したが、低リソース言語では識別性能が全体的に弱く、較正の有用性が損なわれる問題も指摘される。さらに、尤度幾何学に基づき、事実証拠方向に沿って英語の強い証拠を選択的にアラインさせることで、ターゲット言語のラベルなしで識別性能と事実生成を改善する手法も提案している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMのハルシネーション対策と信頼度較正に直結する手法

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility
papers.summary: Muon has emerged as a strong optimizer for neural network training and admits an interpretation as steepest descent under a spectral-norm geometry. Yet we find that Muon-trained Transformers can degrade sharply when their MLP hidden channels are pruned after training. To reconcile Muon's optimization performance with structured compressibility, we introduce Budget Muon (BMuon), which modifies Muon's spectral geometry so that hidden channels across blocks compete for a shared allocation budget. The resulting oracle is exactly normalized steepest descent under a family of norms that interpolate between Muon's geometry and structured sparse geometries. Our principal sparsity control is an interpretable global channel-allocation budget, rather than a setting-dependent sparsity-penalty coefficient. For linear factorization models, we show that Muon admits minimum-cost exact representations with redundant hidden width, whereas under the BMuon oracle geometry and a sufficiently scarce budget, every minimum-cost representation is width-minimal. For practical training, we derive a minorization-maximization surrogate for the exact allocation problem. On ImageNet-1K with ViT-S/16, BMuon improves over Muon under gradual structured MLP pruning, and its learned allocations provide a more effective pruning criterion than weight magnitude. On a 1B-parameter LLaMA-style model trained on FineWeb, BMuon improves over Muon under post-training MLP channel pruning.
papers.title_ja: BMuon: 構造化圧縮性のためのMuonのスペクトル幾何学予算化
papers.summary_ja: Muonオプティマイザは訓練性能が高いが、訓練後のMLPチャネル剪定で性能が低下する問題がある。本論文は、ブロック間の隠れ層チャネルが共有予算を競い合うように幾何学を修正したBMuonを提案する。これにより、冗長な幅を持つ表現ではなく、幅最小の表現を導出する理論的保証が得られる。ViTおよびLLaMAスタイルモデルにおいて、従来の重み大小区分より効果的な剪定基準となり、構造化剪定時の性能低下を抑制する。

papers.title: Evaluating Predictor-Corrector Dependence in Hard-Constrained Climate Emulators
papers.summary: Climate emulators often enforce physical constraints by correcting each state predicted by a neural network, but evaluating only the corrected forecast conflates predictor skill with the effect of the correction. We introduce an evaluation framework that separates these contributions by comparing corrected forecasts, pre-correction predictions along corrected trajectories, and autonomous rollouts with correction disabled. We further cross correction during training and inference to distinguish its immediate effect from how it shapes the learned predictor, and use matched nonphysical controls to test whether improvements are specific to the physical correction. In ACE2, correction substantially improves physical consistency. In a three-seed ACE2 pilot, models trained with correction produce less accurate uncorrected precipitation forecasts at short horizons than models trained without correction, but more accurate forecasts at 10 and 30 days. This contradicts our preregistered hypothesis that the deficit would grow with forecast horizon. In a separate nine-seed experiment, directly supervising the uncorrected output reverses its precipitation forecast deficit at 72 hours while maintaining the accuracy of corrected forecasts at 24 hours. In ConCerNet's heat-equation system, projection-trained models have higher uncorrected trajectory-based vector-field RMSE than models trained without projection, while restoring the physical projection recovers accuracy far more effectively than a matched nonphysical control. Together, these results show that hard corrections can reshape the predictors trained alongside them, creating dependencies that are not visible from corrected forecasts alone. Hard-constrained emulators should therefore be evaluated by separately measuring predictor accuracy, correction effects, and their interaction during training.
papers.title_ja: 硬制約気候エミュレータにおける予測子-補正子の依存関係の評価
papers.summary_ja: ニューラルネットワークによる気候予測において、物理的制約を強制する補正処理と予測モデル自体の性能を分離して評価するフレームワークを提案する。訓練時の補正が予測子の学習に与える影響を分析し、補正なしの予測精度が短期的には低下するが長期的には改善されるという逆説的な現象を発見した。また、非物理的な対照実験を通じて、物理的補正がモデルの軌道安定性に与える固有の効果を実証している。

papers.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
papers.summary: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.

papers.title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
papers.summary: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. Inspired by the optical-networking experience with quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, this article asks when a quantum controller should compute fidelity analytically, simulate it, or learn a surrogate model. The optical analogy is useful but incomplete: optical QoT estimation often predicts a scalar transmission margin, whereas quantum QoT estimation must account for probabilistic entanglement generation, random memory waiting times, decoherence, state consumption, and measurement constraints that can make fidelity a stochastic target. We propose a compute/simulate/learn framework for quantum QoT estimation and illustrate it with a simulation-based proof of concept. Our study shows that analytical composition can be sufficient in simple regimes, that simulation becomes necessary when stochastic memory effects shape the delivered fidelity distribution, and that lightweight learned surrogates can approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost for online control. We close with open challenges for deployment, including stochastic targets, sim-to-real transfer, data-generation cost, physics-informed learning, and generalization beyond individual paths to full network topologies.
papers.title_ja: 量子ネットワークにおける伝送品質推定：計算、シミュレーション、それとも学習か？
papers.summary_ja: 量子ネットワークの制御において、エンタングルメントの忠実度（QoT）を推定する手法として、解析計算・シミュレーション・機械学習サロゲートの使い分けを提案する。光ネットワークとの類似性を踏まえつつ、確率的なメモリ待機やデコヒーレンスなど量子特有の要因を考慮した枠組みを提示する。シミュレーションベースの実証により、単純な環境では解析計算で十分だが、確率的効果が強い場合はシミュレーションが必要、オンライン制御では軽量な学習サロゲートが低コストで有効であることを示す。最後に、物理情報学習やシミュレーションから実環境への転移など、実運用に向けた課題を議論する。

papers.title: Time-Domain Data-Driven Loewner Reduced-Order Models for Electromagnetic Simulation
papers.summary: This paper presents a data-driven Loewner framework for constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) from time-domain electromagnetic (EM) simulation data. High-fidelity simulation of microwave devices can be computationally expensive, particularly when fine spatial discretization and long observation windows are required. The proposed method uses transient input-output data to construct Loewner and shifted Loewner matrices, from which a reduced descriptor realization is obtained through singular value decomposition (SVD). The resulting models are identified from a limited training window and used to predict responses over substantially longer time intervals, with prediction windows up to 50 times the duration of the training window. The method is formalized as an explicit, reproducible algorithm and validated against full-order simulations for four microwave structures: a substrate-integrated-waveguide filter, a frequency-selective surface, an evanescent-mode coaxial comb-line filter, and a diplexer. The results demonstrate the potential of Loewner-based identification to provide compact models of electromagnetic responses while reducing the need for repeated full-order simulation.
papers.title_ja: 電磁気シミュレーションのための時域データ駆動型ローワー縮約モデル
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、時域電磁気シミュレーションデータから縮約モデル（ROM）を構築するデータ駆動型ローワーフレームワークを提案する。過渡入出力データを用いてローワー行列を構築し、特異値分解（SVD）により縮約された記述子実現を得る手法である。限られた学習ウィンドウからモデルを同定し、最大50倍の長い時間区間での応答予測が可能であることを示した。マイクロ波デバイス4種に対する検証により、フルオーダーシミュレーションの繰り返しを減らしつつコンパクトなモデルを提供できることを実証している。

papers.title: When the implementation matters more than the algorithm: NSGA-II and other multi-objective optimizers in engineering design tools
papers.summary: Engineering design tools increasingly embed optimizers as ready-made components that users select by algorithm name, while operator settings and bound, integer and duplicate handling stay fixed inside each tool. This study tests whether the name predicts the result. A tool-agnostic harness exposes one deterministic black box, an emulator of a published 22-variable mixed-integer building-performance problem, to the native optimizers of three Grasshopper plug-ins, to canonical NSGA-II, SMS-EMOA and GDE3 from Python libraries, and to the model-based RBFMOpt. Eighteen configurations were run at 5,000 evaluations under three population allocations, with statistics fixed in advance. Four NSGA-II implementations differed by up to 5% in hypervolume, more than three canonical algorithms of different families differed from one another, and their response to population size differed by up to 10 percentage points; for two MOEA/D implementations, by 28. On ZDT test functions the same NSGA-II implementations differed up to 470-fold in IGD. An ablation in one open-source NSGA-II reproduced the behaviour of one tool from its documented settings but not the gaps of the other two, so documented parameters do not identify an implementation. Counting the budget in wall-clock time reversed the ranking of the model-based optimizer, and reporting the final population instead of the archive understated some configurations by up to a third; most differences fell below the surrogate's error. For optimizers embedded in design-support systems, the implementation is part of the method; a reporting checklist is derived: implementation and version, effective settings, budget in time and evaluations, and archive-based indicators.

papers.title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning
papers.summary: When a fact becomes harder to elicit from a language model, has the model lost it, or has it merely become less accessible? Parameter-updating test-time continual learning agents are usually evaluated by current output accuracy; we ask whether that measurement captures how prior experience shapes later updates. We test whether learning a specific factual binding produces a later relearning advantage beyond familiarity with its entity, answer vocabulary, format, or query slot. In Qwen2.5-1.5B, we compare three matched, counterbalanced histories: LEARNED receives the correct binding, CONTROL receives matched exposure without it, and WRONG receives a competing relation-valid answer in the same slot. After an identical rehearsal-free continual fine-tuning stream, LEARNED reacquires the target faster than CONTROL at a prespecified checkpoint of partial forgetting. WRONG shows no positive advantage over CONTROL, while its comparison with LEARNED provides slot-matched corroboration, subject to possible competitor interference. The advantage remains positive after adjustment for measured pre-relearning behavior. In a secondary descriptive conversion using an unpaired never-seen pool, prior learning reduces the optimizer updates required for restoration by about 18%. Current behavioral accuracy can therefore underestimate the lasting effect of previously acquired experience. Code is available at https://github.com/zhezhou1106/relearning-savings
papers.title_ja: テストタイム継続学習における結合特異的な再学習節約効果
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、LLMのテストタイム継続学習において、特定の事実結合を学習した経験が後の再学習速度に与える影響を定量的に評価する。Qwen2.5-1.5Bを用い、正解結合を学習した群、対照群、誤った結合を学習した群を比較し、忘却後の再獲得速度を測定した。結果、正解結合を学習した群は対照群より再学習が速く、最適化更新回数を約18%削減できることが示された。現在の出力精度だけでは、過去の経験がもたらす潜在的な学習効率化効果を過小評価している可能性がある。

papers.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline
papers.summary: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail. The pattern holds for thirteen released pairs up to 8B parameters, and it is not a mark of alignment: with training held fixed, instruction data does not stand out from Wikipedia or code, DPO gives the same update whether its preference labels are real or half swapped at random (one model, modest preference strength), and scrambled text gives the most concentrated update of all. Applied to a recent claim that post-training is superficial because the effective rank of the weights barely changes, the baselines show that a random update of the same size leaves that rank almost unchanged while wrecking the model, and that an edit built on the effective rank of the update has no measurable effect in our tests. Rank measures of weight updates need a noise baseline, and claims about alignment need a control without alignment content.
papers.title_ja: ファインチューニング更新のランク測定にはノイズベースラインが必要
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、LLMのファインチューニングによる重み更新のランク（次元）を評価する際、ランダム行列などのノイズベースラインと比較する重要性を指摘する。13組のモデル（最大8Bパラメータ）で検証した結果、更新は少数の強い方向と長いテールからなり、アライメント内容の有無やデータの種類（Wikipedia、コード等）によってランク特性が大きく変わらないことが判明した。また、既存研究が主張する「ポストトレーニングは表面的である」という見解に対し、ランダム更新でもランクはほぼ不変だがモデル性能は崩壊するため、ランク単独での解釈は誤りであることを示した。したがって、重み更新のランク測定には適切なノイズ基準、アライメント効果の主張にはアライメント内容を含まない対照実験が不可欠である。

papers.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
papers.summary: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.
papers.title_ja: Lean4AgenticRL: 検証可能な多層プロセス報酬によるエージェント型強化学習の推進
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMのエージェント能力を高めるための強化学習フレームワーク「Lean4AgenticRL」を提案する。従来の成果報酬中心のアプローチに対し、Lean4による形式化を用いてツール呼び出しやワークフロー段階などの多層プロセス報酬を導入し、訓練の効率と有効性を向上させる。この手法を用いて訓練したLAR-9B/27Bモデルは、TerminalBench-2.1で77.3%の高精度を達成し、同規模の既存モデルを上回る性能を示した。形式手法と強化学習の統合により、オープンエンドなエージェントタスクにおける推論と行動の検証可能性を高めることを実証している。

papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.summary: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., {\pi}0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

papers.title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. However, prior work largely treats PI as a fixed design choice, leaving the effects of its content and construction poorly understood. This challenge is particularly important in multi-turn agentic settings, where trajectories contain actions, observations, and reasoning that can be transformed into PI in many ways. We systematically evaluate 16 PI configurations across three multi-turn agentic benchmarks and three student models that vary in scale and reasoning mode. We find that PI effectiveness depends on its content, generation source, and the student model. Information-dense trajectories and PI produced by more capable generators generally yield larger gains, whereas thinking models benefit less consistently. To assess PI before training, we compare PI utility with two KL-based metrics: sampled-token reverse KL ($D$) and error-step KL contrast ($\Delta d^{-}_{\mathrm{err}}$). The KL-based metrics track post-training performance more consistently than PI utility, which can be distorted by information leakage. Empirically, selecting each task's PI by $\Delta d^{-}_{\mathrm{err}}$ also improves post-training performance over random selection, most when the PI candidates differ widely. Finally, effective PI remains beneficial when combined with GRPO, allowing the combined objective to outperform a strong GRPO baseline. Overall, our results provide practical guidance for constructing and evaluating PI in OPSD training.
papers.title_ja: オンポリシー自己蒸留における特権情報の有効性予測

papers.title: Can LLMs predict the outcomes of machine learning experiments?
papers.summary: Recent advances in AI make Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) increasingly plausible. Large Language Models (LLMs) can already propose, select, and run Machine Learning (ML) experiments. However, the space of possible design choices in ML is vast. An LLM that proposes an experiment needs a reliable intuition of whether it is worth running given the timing constraints of long training runs. In this work, we measure such intuition in current frontier LLMs by evaluating how accurately they predict the impact of self-generated ML experiment ideas before these are put into training runs. To this end, we construct a dataset of 288 LLM-proposed ideas on eight MLE-bench tasks. We then prompt five frontier LLMs (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.3) to predict the impact of each idea and compare their predictions with the actual outcomes after training. We report four main findings. First, LLM predictions are substantially better than random chance but far from accurate: even the best model, Claude Opus 5.5, explains only half of the variance in outcomes (R^2 = 0.49). Second, we notice that all tested models systematically underestimate the magnitude of the changes. Third, prediction quality varies widely across tasks. Finally, the choice of the coding harness that actually implements the ideas has little effect on outcomes, and we find no evidence of self-preference. Higher reasoning settings and additional context lead to modest gains. Overall, our results show that current LLMs have useful but limited intuition about which ML ideas will work. We release our dataset to support further study.

papers.title: Noise-shaped Sampling and Annealing for Scalable On-the-edge Training of Binary and Ternary AI Models
papers.summary: The training loss of binary and ternary neural networks, expanded as a multilinear polynomial over the discrete weights, is structurally equivalent to the energy of a hierarchical high-order Ising model. We exploit this equivalence to apply Ising solvers to discrete-weight network training, while accounting for a fundamental difference in objectives: an Ising solver seeks the ground state of a fixed energy function, whereas training seeks solutions that generalize to unseen data. Our key contribution is $\Sigma\Delta$-Sampler, an optimizer that reconciles these objectives by embedding a stochastic sampling-and-annealing step as a noisy quantizer inside a first-order $\Sigma\Delta$ noise-shaping loop. The loop pushes noise from weight quantization, high-order frustration, and mini-batch sampling out of the low-frequency adaptation band, so that discrete weight updates follow the smooth descent trajectories embedded in the rugged loss landscape. We validate the framework on a planted quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) benchmark with a known minimizer; on CIFAR-10, where a $13$M-parameter ternary model comes within $1\%$ of full-precision accuracy; on ImageNet-1k, where a ternary ResNet-18 comes within $0.4\%$ Top-5 accuracy of a ternary baseline; on class-incremental continual learning, where prior-task accuracy is preserved; and on MatMul-free language models up to $2.7$B parameters, where it outperforms a straight-through-estimator baseline under matched continued pre-training. Compared with standard quantization-aware training, $\Sigma\Delta$-Sampler reduces the training memory footprint by over $50\%$, delivers an order-of-magnitude speed-up, and reduces weight-update memory traffic by four orders of magnitude, making it attractive for on-device training and fine-tuning of large binary and ternary models.

papers.title: The Ephemeral Cost of Switching Optimizers Across LLM Training Stages
papers.summary: Recent work suggests that switching optimizers between pretraining and subsequent training stages incurs a performance cost, but systematic investigation of this phenomenon is lacking. We study the mismatch between AdamW and Muon optimizers by pretraining 1.2B Llama-3 models from scratch while varying the proportion of updates taken with each optimizer, and similarly interpolating between the two optimizers during continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Surprisingly, we find little evidence of a meaningful optimizer mismatch penalty: final performance is largely explained by the independent effects of the pretraining and post-training optimizers, with downstream performance generally improving as the proportion of Muon updates during SFT increases. Although matching the pretraining optimizer can reduce forgetting during SFT, this does not translate into improved final benchmark performance. We further evaluate AdamW and Muon for task-general SFT of open-weight models, across the Llama and Qwen families up to 14B parameters, where Muon remains competitive with AdamW, despite these models having been pretrained with AdamW. Together, our results suggest that the choice of optimizer for post-training can be made largely independently of the optimizer used during pretraining.
papers.title_ja: LLM学習段階間でオプティマイザを切り替える際の一時的なコスト

papers.title: Edit Discovery in Human-AI Interactions
papers.summary: Human-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool-use overhead. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions while controlling unnecessary confirmations and respecting an editor-cost budget. We characterize the population-optimal policy and show that it takes the form of a cost-adjusted threshold on the posterior probability of an edit. Building on this structure, we develop EDIT (Edit Discovery via Iterative Thresholding), an online algorithm for the partial-feedback setting in which edit labels are revealed only for selected interactions. EDIT combines an adaptive edit score, a confirmation-control threshold, and a cost-aware selection rule; it satisfies the editor budget at every round and controls the average confirmation rate up to a vanishing finite-horizon term, without distributional assumptions on the interaction stream. Across four reasoning and factual question-answering benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade-off between editor cost, Type-I error, and Type-II error than direct LLM-based batch selection.

papers.title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
papers.summary: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. Yet outcome-based training of Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop. We introduce AlphaBet, an agentic reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates. Each dated forecast is scored by a proper scoring rule against the eventual outcome, allowing one resolved event to supervise decisions under different information states. We decompose forecasting regret into an evidence-acquisition gap and a probability-reporting gap, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)'s standard-deviation normalization can distort the reporting target under multi-class proper scores. On GLM-4.5-Air, AlphaBet reduces the Brier score from 0.731 to 0.626 on Forecast-Dojo and from 0.612 to 0.528 on FutureX. Controlled ablations attribute these gains to multi-date training and show that they come from improvements in both information acquisition and probability reporting. Our empirical results validate that GRPO's std normalization degrades proper-scoring-rule performance while leaving top-outcome accuracy largely unchanged.
papers.title_ja: AlphaBet: LLMイベント予測エージェントのための強化学習
papers.summary_ja: 未解決イベントの予測において、証拠の収集から確率報告までを単一のLLMポリシーで学習する強化学習フレームワーク「AlphaBet」を提案する。複数時点での予測を適切なスコアリングルールで評価し、証拠取得と確率報告の両方のギャップを最適化する。GRPOの標準偏差正規化がマルチクラススコアリング下で性能を劣化させることを示し、これを修正することでBrierスコアを大幅に改善した。Forecast-DojoおよびFutureXベンチマークにおいて、情報取得と確率報告の両面で既存手法を上回る性能を実証した。

papers.title: Chance-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning
papers.summary: We study personalized LLM routing, where a router selects among heterogeneous models with different costs and capabilities. The router must minimize cumulative inference cost while ensuring reliable realized response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned from feedback during deployment. We formulate this problem as a constrained contextual bandit and develop an algorithm that learns preferences while balancing cost and quality. Under a logistic preference model and a strict-feasibility condition, we establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized contextual oracle and a high-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction. The framework extends beyond LLM routing to broader online model-selection problems with reliability requirements.
papers.title_ja: オンライン嗜好学習を用いた確率制約付きパーソナライズドLLMルーティング
papers.summary_ja: コストと能力が異なる複数のLLMから、ユーザーの嗜好をオンラインで学習しながら最適なモデルを選択するルーティング問題を研究する。この問題を制約付きコンテキストバンディットとして定式化し、コスト最小化と回答品質の信頼性を両立させるアルゴリズムを提案する。ロジスティック嗜好モデルの下で、期待コストのレグレットが亜線形であることを示し、実現される累積満足度に対する高確率保証を導出する。本フレームワークはLLMルーティングに限らず、信頼性要件を持つオンラインモデル選択問題全般に拡張可能である。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論コスト最適化とオンライン学習手法の組み合わせが関心に直結

papers.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.
papers.title_ja: CoLU: 大規模言語モデルにおける信頼度重み付きレイヤー別アンラーニング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMのアンラーニング（特定情報の忘却）において、モデル全体ではなく単一のトランスフォーマーレイヤーのみを更新する手法CoLUを提案する。信頼度重み付きの忘却・保持正則化を用いることで、忘却と知識保持のトレードオフを改善する。さらに、簡易なスクリーニング手法BLSにより計算コストを最大79.7%削減しつつ、既存手法を上回る性能を達成した。GPUメモリ使用量も大幅に低減され、効率的なアンラーニングを実現する。

papers.title: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high-stakes settings. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive. A well-known and efficient class of monitors can detect such failures from internal representations (such as activation probes), but are tied to the model they were trained on, requiring costly re-annotation as new LLMs appear. A natural way to avoid this repeated annotation cost is to develop internal-representation based monitors that transfer zero-shot across LLMs. However, such transfer is challenging because internal representations are not naturally aligned across models; in particular, attention maps, known to contain signals of misbehavior, may differ in head function, ordering, and model depth. In this work, we characterize those cross-model attention mismatches as algebraic symmetries and use geometric deep learning principles to build LEMON (Language-model Equivariant MOnitoring Network) an online graph neural network-based monitor, whose predictions are invariant under these symmetries. LEMON processes attention maps token-by-token, as they are produced and outputs a score after every token (or every window of $W$ tokens) at negligible cost. Across 16 LLMs and six datasets, in the zero-shot cross-model setting, LEMON outperforms all baselines on both hallucination and jailbreak monitoring tasks, improving over the strongest by up to 14 ROC-AUC points.
papers.title_ja: LEMON: 新LLMにおけるゼロショット悪意ある行動監視のためのアテンションマップ上での等変学習
papers.summary_ja: 外部LLM監視のコストやモデル依存性を解消するため、アテンションマップの代数対称性を活用した等変グラフニューラルネットワーク「LEMON」を提案する。この手法はモデル間のアテンション構造の不一致を幾何学的に処理し、新しいLLMでも再学習なしでゼロショット転移を実現する。トークンごとにオンラインでスコアを出力し、ハルシネーションやジェイルブレイクの監視において既存手法を上回る性能を示した。

papers.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
papers.summary: LLM safety evaluations via jailbreaking typically index on attack success rate (ASR): whether a generated response violates safeguards. However, ASR only evaluates sampled outputs and provides little information on the underlying generation process. Autoregressive language models define distributions over possible outputs, and a sampled refusal can coexist with substantial probability mass on harmful generation paths. We study this hidden structure through bounded continuation analysis (BCA), which models autoregressive generation as a stochastic process over token prefixes and computes the finite-horizon probability that generation reaches a harmful continuation. BCA constructs a bounded continuation tree, labels terminal continuations with a semantic harm evaluator, and estimates harmful reachability using exact probabilistic model checking. BCA complements ASR by measuring how much harmful behavior remains accessible beneath a sampled safe response. This makes it useful for distinguishing models that look identical under measured ASR values, and allocating red-team effort toward regions of the generation process with greater hidden risk. Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming.
papers.title_ja: 拒否は堅牢性を意味しない：自動回帰言語モデルにおける有害到達可能性の測定
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMの安全性評価において従来の攻撃成功率（ASR）が捉えきれない「隠れた有害性」を定量化する手法「有界継続分析（BCA）」を提案する。BCAは自動回帰生成を確率過程としてモデル化し、トークン接頭辞上の確率木を用いて有害な継続に到達する有限時間確率を厳密に計算する。これにより、サンプル出力が安全に見えても内部に有害な確率質量が潜んでいる状態を可視化し、ASR値が同一のモデル間のリスク差を識別できる。4つの指示チューニング済みLLMと100のJailbreakBench行動を用いた実験で、BCAがレッドチーミングの効率化に有用なシグナルを提供することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの安全性評価・ハルシネーション対策に直結する手法

papers.title: Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations
papers.summary: Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group-wise gains and installs them in the recipient's weights or native quantization scales without recipient-side optimization. On a quantized recipient, it preserves integer codes, zero points and storage layout. For a Qwen3-1.7B floating-point/GPTQ INT3 pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76.9-90.5% of the text-loss improvement from recipient-specific calibration on fresh WikiText and C4 cohorts excluded from project development. Shuffling the same gain values within each projection worsens both recipients, showing that their learned group assignment matters after transfer. A Llama-3.2-3B control keeps the initial native tensors at all four calibrated projections identical and changes nine projections elsewhere. Cross-installation retains 98.6-99.3% of the text-calibration benefit, alongside a small, resolved preference for each recipient's own gain. These results quantify both the adaptation carried by a reusable calibration update and the remaining benefit of recipient-specific training.
papers.title_ja: モデル表現間のキャリブレーション利得の再利用
papers.summary_ja: 同一事前学習モデルの異なる表現間（例：浮動小数点と量子化版）で、キャリブレーションによる更新利得を転用する手法を提案する。受信側モデルの重みや量子化スケールに正のグループワイズ利得をインストールし、受信側での最適化計算を不要にする。Qwen3-1.7Bの浮動小数点/GPTQ INT3ペアにおいて、双方向転用で受信側固有キャリブレーションの76.9〜90.5%のテキスト損失改善を維持した。また、利得のグループ割り当てが重要であること、およびLlama-3.2-3Bでは98.6〜99.3%の利得を保持できることを示し、再利用可能な適応成分と固有学習の残存利得を定量化した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化・効率化と推論高速化に直結する手法

papers.title: Physics-Transfer Learning: A Physics-Constrained Theory for Zero-Shot Generalization Along the Ladder of Complexity
papers.summary: Reliable out-of-distribution generalization remains a central challenge in machine learning, particularly when models are deployed in data-scarce high-fidelity domains. Existing approaches often rely on statistical distribution alignment, or invariance assumptions that can fail when domain shifts reflect changes in underlying mechanisms. Inspired by a longstanding paradigm in physics that understands complex systems by starting from tractable idealizations and progressively incorporating additional mechanisms and levels of fidelity, we propose physics-transfer (PT) learning, a physics-constrained learning theory for zero-shot generalization along a ladder of complexity. PT constructs chains of anchor domains (CADs) that connect low-cost source domains to complex targets and introduces computable feasibility and reliability indicators for assessing transfer before target-domain labels are observed. Under physical-consistency and stable-representation assumptions, we derive an operational upper bound on target risk in terms of source empirical risk, the PT indicators, and finite-sample errors, and establish convergence as adjacent complexity gaps shrink and data coverage improves. We evaluate PT on excited-state energy prediction in quantum systems and dynamical-transition prediction in classical systems using neural networks trained without target-domain labels. Across substantial distribution shifts, PT yields accurate high-fidelity predictions, while the indicators identify incorrect physical mappings before target-domain prediction fails. These results provide a model-agnostic framework for designing, diagnosing, and controlling generalization in data-scarce learning problems.
papers.title_ja: 物理転移学習：複雑さの階層に沿ったゼロショット汎化のための物理制約理論
papers.summary_ja: データが乏しい高忠実度領域における分布外汎化を改善するため、物理的な複雑さの階層（ラダー）に沿ったゼロショット転移学習フレームワークを提案する。低コストなソースドメインからターゲットドメインへ繋ぐアンカードメインの連鎖を構築し、ターゲットラベルなしで転移の信頼性を評価する指標を導入する。物理的一貫性と安定表現の仮定のもと、ターゲットリスクの上限を導出し、量子系の励起状態エネルギー予測や古典系の動的遷移予測において、既存手法を上回る精度と誤った物理マッピングの検出能力を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理制約とサロゲートモデルの汎化理論であり、MLと物理の融合に直結

papers.title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion
papers.summary: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens during training. At inference, a heuristic sampler re-injects noise into suspicious context under an annealed intensity and freezes context updates late in the trajectory. An 8,000-step finetune of a pretrained 170M-parameter masked diffusion model takes under five hours on a 6 GB laptop GPU. The base model assigns roughly 50% probability to observed tokens even when they are uniform-random garbage. For uniform-random corruption, finetuning detects corrupted context with 0.96 recall and 0.91 precision, improves infill token-F1 by 3.8 points at 10% corruption and 6.4 points at 20%, and removes the accuracy dip next to corruptions. Clean conditioning shows no measurable regression, with a false-edit rate below 0.4%. Gains for plausible corruptions are weaker: about 0.5 F1 points at 10% corruption, without statistical significance. Our results suggest that detectability and damage depend jointly on departure from the data conditional: nearby noise is hard to detect and semantically mild, while distant noise is conspicuous and destructive. We interpret absorbing diffusion as the infinite-contrast limit of a trust axis, analogous to the signal-to-noise gap between known and unknown regions in diffusion inpainting. In our setting of a 170M model and a single text domain, intermediate trust is reached by changing forward dynamics rather than architecture.
papers.title_ja: 信頼するが検証する：離散拡散における領域非均質フォワードダイナミクスの設計
papers.summary_ja: 離散拡散モデルにおいて、コンテキストを完全に信頼する従来の手法の限界を指摘し、欠損位置とコンテキストに異なるノイズ動態を適用する「領域非均質フォワードダイナミクス」を提案する。推論時に疑わしいコンテキストへノイズを再注入するヒューリスティックなサンプラーを導入し、誤ったコンテキストの検出と生成品質の向上を実現した。170Mパラメータのモデルを6GBのGPUで数時間以内にファインチューニング可能であり、ランダムな破損に対して高い検出率とF1スコアの改善を示す一方、妥当な破損への効果は限定的である。本研究は、信頼度の軸をフォワードダイナミクスで制御することで、ハルシネーションや誤情報伝播への対策として有効であることを示唆している。

papers.title: TRACE: Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding for Communication-efficient Distributed Edge Inference
papers.summary: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. Existing compression schemes reduce this cost but retain a structural bottleneck: the received data must still undergo key/value projection before attention can proceed, serializing computation behind communication. This paper presents Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding (Trace), a framework that addresses these limitations. Trace places a Vector Quantizer (VQ) at the post-attention residual of every Transformer layer and precomputes codebook-indexed key/value representations. During inference, exchanged activations are encoded into compact codebook indices, allowing receivers to directly recover keys and values through table lookup instead of executing the downstream computations required to derive them. By eliminating the received data downstream computation, Trace enables communication--computation overlap and reduces a key latency bottleneck in distributed Transformer inference. A hierarchical clustering further structures the learned codebook into a multi-resolution hierarchy, enabling runtime adaptation of the communication bitrate without retraining. The framework supports two operating variants: one prioritizing accuracy and the other balancing accuracy and efficiency through buffer-compatible quantization. Experiments on ViT-Base (ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100) and ViViT-B (UCF-101) show that Trace achieves up to 1.89% higher accuracy and up to 1.27x end-to-end inference speedup compared with the state-of-the-art VQ-based distributed inference framework. Compared with uncompressed sequence-parallel inference, Trace reduces communication overhead by up to 22,624x.
papers.title_ja: TRACE: 通信効率化のための分散エッジ推論向けTransformer残差活性化コードブック符号化
papers.summary_ja: 分散エッジデバイスにおけるTransformer推論の通信ボトルネックを解決するフレームワーク「Trace」を提案する。アテンション後の残差にベクトル量子化（VQ）を適用し、コードブックインデックスとしてアクティベーションを伝送することで、受信側でのKey/Value投影計算を省略し、通信と計算のオーバーラップを実現する。階層クラスタリングにより学習不要で通信ビットレート適応が可能であり、ViTモデルを用いた実験では既存手法比で最大1.27倍の推論高速化と、非圧縮比で最大22,624倍の通信オーバーヘッド削減を達成した。

papers.title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
papers.summary: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? We develop four executable operations for changing physical descriptions: identifying redundancies (L1), coarse-graining dynamics (L2), transferring structure (L3), and inferring missing quantities from conservation imbalances (L4). We evaluate these operations and three interpretability settings through null acceptance (NAR), positive acceptance (PAR), and consequence agreement (CAR). A reduction mapping every state to zero predicts its own future perfectly. It passes closure on 96% of 129 public chaotic systems despite retaining no dynamical variation. An independent observable-preservation test rejects it throughout. On controlled benchmarks, the combined criteria accept 24/24 genuine reductions and reject 72/72 nulls. The other operations distinguish symmetries from redundancies, validate transfers, and reject spurious conservation imbalances. In language and ESM-2 protein models, linear CKA remains unchanged when a proposed correspondence is randomly rotated, whereas localized interventions distinguish genuine mappings from tested nulls. In sparse autoencoders, enrichment rejects all 16 tested nulls, yet independent ablation supports 45% of evaluable enriched features, compared with 0.5% of matched controls. These results reveal two acceptance gaps: descriptive tests can accept scientifically empty candidates, and accepted candidates can lack independently verified consequences. Reliable automated discovery requires evaluating both what a test accepts and the scientific consequences it establishes. Code and data: https://real-project-aether.github.io/project-aether/.
papers.title_ja: ヌルコントロールは必要だが十分ではない：科学的発見と解釈可能性における受容ガードの評価
papers.summary_ja: 自動発見システムが提案する科学的説明の受容基準を評価し、単なる記述的テストでは科学的に空虚な候補も受容してしまう「受容ギャップ」を指摘する。カオス系やタンパク質モデル、スパースオートエンコーダを用い、独立した検証テスト（PAR, CAR）が偽陽性を排除し、真の構造変換や対応関係を識別できることを示す。特に、状態をゼロに縮約するヌルモデルが96%の系でクローズドテストを通過するものの、観測可能量保存テストで拒否される事例を通じて、科学的結果の独立検証の重要性を実証している。
